mr_title: feat(v4): parse input containing reference cycles
mr_description:
Today a cyclic input is a RangeError, safeParse included, so it isn't
even catchable through the result.

Core gains a $ZodMemoizer seam: a container asks the injected memoizer
for the object it is about to build into. Classic injects one per
container instance; zod/mini injects nothing and links none of this.
Core's whole share is one interface, one `_zod` field, one changed
allocation line per container, and one line in runChecks -- the memoizer
is read once at construction, so a schema without one runs exactly the
code it runs today, and the JIT emits byte-identical output for it.

Everything else lives in core/memoizer.ts, which nothing references
unless a layer asks for it. It registers the real output object before
any child is parsed, so a reference back to the same input resolves to
it with nothing to copy. The lookup is keyed on (schema, input), which
is what makes mutual recursion sound: a node validated against two
schemas gets an output per schema. A repeat visit returns without
reaching core, which also stops the node's checks running against a
half-built value. A cycle closing through a transform throws
ZodCyclicError. A schema that cannot re-enter itself removes the
interceptor on its first parse.

expected_issues.title: Cycle detection reads getters and calls user default factories
expected_issues.description:
isRecursive() reads every enumerable property of a schema def, and `.default(fn)` exposes defaultValue as a getter that calls the user's factory, so the factory runs during the cycle walk (on first parse, even when the key is present, and at compile time).

The generic `for...in` scan of def assumes plain data properties. Default factories are commonly used for side-effecting or unique values (new Date(), randomUUID(), counters); invoking them from an introspection walk produces extra calls and observable side effects that did not exist before. The walk must enumerate schema-bearing slots explicitly or skip accessor properties.
